name: agent-mcp-multiplexer
description: Tier-P F1 process-topology scenario: install ONLY agent-mcp on a fresh box, provision the runtime, then drive N `agent-mcp forward` sessions against a stdio-echo upstream and assert the #744 multiplexer's process TOPOLOGY deterministically -- exactly one resident `serve` host plus N thin forwarders (never N heavy bridges), each session still answering `initialize`/`tools/list` correctly through it. Also asserts the always-optional direct-bridge fallback (`AGENT_MCP_NO_MULTIPLEX=1` spawns zero resident hosts) and the host's idle self-eviction (a short-`--idle-timeout` host exits once its last attached session detaches). FIDELITY: the RAM footprint delta is already proven by `plugins/agent-mcp/examples/multiplexer_ab.py` (a Linux /proc A/B); this scenario proves the discrete TOPOLOGY invariant (one host, not N) the RAM win depends on, plus the fallback and eviction properties. The heavy assertions live in a portable, stdlib-only probe (`fixtures/multiplexer_topology_probe.py`, Linux/proc-based like the A/B script) so it is verifiable off-Docker too. Follow-up from the plugin-process-hygiene effort's #744 multiplexer slices (#866). Name-free / public.
